intent: Preserve attempt IDs referenced by retained canonical samples and events when legacy history lacks a separate attempt row; exclude only incoming components that alias that known ownership.
constraints: Retain existing row-based attempt IDs, original canonical payload bytes, transaction boundaries, pending-owner deletion guard and ordinary/settled replacement behavior.
Do not reconstruct absent rows or broaden restore refusal policy.
No root or foreign worktree edits and no remote writes.
supported_states: Store.save and legacy run-only backup decoding accept a pending sample without a separate batch/attempt/event row.
Backup decoding accepts retained batch-event attempt references independently of optional attempt rows and sample attemptId fields.

validation.initial_probe: Exact b715 ownership helper compiles; one isolated regression fails because original-attempt is imported under foreign-batch/foreign-run/foreign-request while the original pending sample remains.

regression_suite.boundary: Exact current ownership helper, cleanup predicate and attempt receipt compiled with actual fixture and byte-matched production domain models; unused platform/native/audit dependencies remain host boundaries.

validation.canonical_validation: Parent integration owns canonical and final-head hosted gates.
validation.limits: Actual ownership helper and pending predicate with byte-matched production domain models; no new Store/Room or complete Android execution claim.
validation.formatting: Pinned ktlint1.3.1 and git diff --check passed.
validation.independent_review: Read-only peer review clear: added IDs originate only in the existing retained canonical component; incoming data cannot seed retention; transaction, receipt bytes and settled/no-owner fast path remain unchanged.

behavior: Retain original canonical run/batch/queue/attempt/event bytes and all existing row-based ownership.
Sample or event references establish only protected original attempt IDs; missing rows are never reconstructed.
Imported conflicts still use the existing connected-component exclusion, while ordinary and confirmed-settled replacement controls are unchanged.
